name: Matt King

nadir.desc: The property consists of a single-story primary residence with a gray shingle roof and attached garage|A concrete driveway leads from a circular cul-de-sac to the garage|One vehicle is parked in the driveway|Landscaping with shrubs and trees surrounds portions of the house|Dense trees line one side of the property adjacent to a road|Open paved areas form the cul-de-sac frontage.

alpha.desc: The front of the residence shows a light-colored single-story house with a gray roof and attached garage|A concrete driveway extends from the cul-de-sac to the garage|One vehicle is parked in the driveway|Landscaping shrubs and trees are present near the front of the house|A wooden fence is visible along one side of the property.

bravo.desc: The left side of the residence shows the side of the house facing a parallel road|Dense trees and vegetation run along this side of the property|The house sits at a higher elevation relative to the adjacent road|A retaining edge or grade change is visible|Limited open space exists between the house and the tree line.

charlie.desc: The rear of the residence is partially screened by dense trees and vegetation|Portions of the house roof and upper walls are visible through the tree cover|The adjacent road runs along the lower edge of the property|A large retaining wall separates the property with the roadside sidewalk|Open space is limited on this side due to the vegetation density.

delta.desc: The right side of the residence shows the side and rear of the gray house|The right side, like the left, shows a steep slope downwards towards the retaining wall|Windows and exterior walls are visible|Dense trees continue along one edge of the property|A paved path or sidewalk area is present near the house|The adjacent road is visible at the lower edge of the lot.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided by a concrete driveway that leads from the circular cul-de-sac directly to the attached garage. The driveway and cul-de-sac offer clear space for vehicle approach and staging. One vehicle is parked in the driveway. Dense trees line the side of the property adjacent to a parallel road, creating a vegetated buffer and potential visibility limitation from that direction. The house sits at a higher elevation than the adjacent road. Neighboring residences are present on the cul-de-sac. A large commercial structure and open fields are located nearby along the highway corridor.
clarifications: Does the attached garage provide direct interior access into the house? Is there any secondary pedestrian or vehicle access from the tree-lined side of the property that faces the parallel road? How dense is the tree cover for movement around the side and rear of the house? Is the wooden fence continuous, or are there gates that allow side access? Can emergency vehicles fully utilize the cul-de-sac and driveway without obstruction from the parked vehicle?
